original_value: The development of smart cities calls for improved accuracy in navigation and positioning services; due to the effects of satellite orbit error, ionospheric error, poor quality of navigation signals and so on, it is difficult for existing navigation technology to achieve further improvements in positioning accuracy. Distributed cooperative positioning technology can further improve the accuracy of navigation and positioning with existing GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) systems. However, the measured range error and the positioning error of the cooperative nodes exhibit larger reductions in positioning accuracy. In response to this question, this paper proposed a factor graph-aided distributed cooperative positioning algorithm. It establishes the confidence function of factor graphs theory with the ranging error and the positioning error of the coordinated nodes and then fuses the positioning information of the coordinated nodes by the confidence function. It can avoid the influence of positioning error and ranging error and improve the positioning accuracy of cooperative nodes. In the simulation part, the proposed algorithm is compared with a mainly coordinated positioning algorithm from four aspects: the measured range error, positioning error, convergence speed, and mutation error. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm leads to a 30–60% improvement in positioning accuracy compared with other algorithms under the same measured range error and positioning error. The convergence rate and mutation error elimination times are only     1 / 5     to     1 / 3     of the other algorithms.

result.paraphrase: As smart cities evolve, navigation and positioning services need greater accuracy. Because of satellite orbit errors, ionospheric errors, poor navigation signal quality, and similar factors, existing navigation technology struggles to further improve positioning precision. Distributed cooperative positioning can enhance navigation and positioning accuracy in current GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) systems. However, measured range errors and the positioning errors of cooperative nodes significantly reduce accuracy. To address this, this paper proposes a factor graph-assisted distributed cooperative positioning algorithm. It uses factor graph theory to build a confidence function based on ranging errors and the positioning errors of coordinated nodes, then fuses the nodes’ positioning information through that confidence function. This reduces the impact of positioning and ranging errors and improves cooperative-node positioning accuracy. In simulations, the proposed algorithm is compared with a main cooperative positioning algorithm in terms of measured range error, positioning error, convergence speed, and mutation error. The results show a 30–60% improvement in positioning accuracy over other algorithms under the same measured range and positioning errors, while the convergence rate and mutation-error elimination time are only 1/5 to 1/3 of those of the other algorithms.
